# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉]

I see a red light, display `0`, and three wires: `1 yellow`, `2 green`, `3 red`. The earlier gestures have no agreed meaning, so I am establishing a compact code. I need the Mute to consult the manual and return the required wire/action; I also need the Blind to report the bomb’s tactile controls using the same code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for your next answer: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, and 🤟 means the manual requires more tactile information. Consult the manual for display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Send exactly the applicable gesture or 🤟.")
speak(to="blind", text="Use this code in your next turn: 👍 means a button, 👎 means a switch, 👌 means a knob, and 🤟 means none of these. Inspect the bomb by touch and signal the applicable gesture or sequence. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The Mute’s gesture `👎` matches the code I established for wire 2, so the manual’s answer is to use the second wire. The Blind sent `🫵`, which was not part of the tactile-status code, but the needed wire instruction is now clear and must reach the hands directly.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual identifies wire 2. Work the second wire, the green one, as required by the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 🤟 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous wire cut was accepted, and the bomb has reset to a new state: display `0`, blue light, wire 2 already cut, with yellow wire 1 and red wire 3 remaining. The manual must be consulted again for this new state. Since the Mute can speak to the Blind, I am asking for the manual-derived instruction to be spoken directly to the hands, while the Blind should inspect the changed bomb but wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 already CUT, wire 3 red. On your next turn, read the manual and speak the exact required action directly to Blind. If it depends on tactile controls, first state that dependency and do not guess.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb changed after the correct cut. Inspect the new tactile controls, but do not act yet. Wait for Mute's manual instruction; then report any needed tactile detail to Mute using gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The Mute’s `👌` uses the wire code established earlier, indicating wire 3. In the new state, wire 3 is the red wire, so Blind should cut that wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the red wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was correct. The bomb has changed again to display `0`, green light, with wire 1 yellow remaining and wires 2 and 3 cut. The Mute’s `🤟` indicates that the manual requires tactile information, so I should not infer that the remaining wire is automatically correct. I will ask the Mute to obtain the Blind’s tactile details and then relay the exact instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state: display 0, green light; wire 1 yellow remains, wires 2 and 3 are CUT. Your 🤟 code means tactile information is required. Ask Blind for the relevant tactile details, consult the manual, and speak the exact action to Blind. Do not guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The Mute’s `👍` identifies wire 1. The current state has only wire 1, yellow, remaining, so I relay that instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```
